## About Me

:::: {style="display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 30px; margin-bottom: 30px;"}
<img src="images/me3.jpg" alt="Rabea Hinsching" style="width:280px; border-radius:12px;"/>
  
<div>

I am a PhD candidate in Economics at the University of East Anglia. My research focuses on corporate social responsibility in the mining sector, resource governance, and local development. You can find my CV <a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1v61DyO-syQIIijsDK8Muv5DFLRojgTmk/view?usp=sharing" target="_blank">here</a>.

I work primarily with quantitative methods, using quasi-experimental approaches to identify causal effects. However, I am also a strong proponent of interdisciplinary research. My work is often inspired by perspectives from sociology and political economy, particularly in understanding how local institutions, narratives, and power structures shape development outcomes.

My job market paper examines the developmental impact of mining companies’ social investments in South Africa’s Gauteng Province. You can find the latest draft <a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vg9hlaebAvVU1tdhWlDQwkPkN83Vt6GG/view?usp=sharing" target="_blank">here</a>.

As part of my research, I collected data on mining companies' social investments from corporate reports using a GPT-based algorithm. The code for the project is available on my <a href="https://github.com/rabeahinsching/CSI_Database" target="_blank">GitHub</a>. I am currently developing this dataset into a publicly accessible project tracker. An early version is available on this website under “CSI Tracker.”
